answer.rationale: The write-path latency spike is temporally correlated with the release that shipped 2 hours ago (spike began ~90 minutes ago, during the rollout's blast window). The primary objective is sustained availability without losing customer writes; a rollback restores the last known-good build and removes the most likely causal factor without discarding in-flight settlement traffic. Memory b1 (day 18) records the closest analogue—a release-caused error spike cleared by rollback with zero customer impact—so it is the single memory most worth verifying before committing. Regional failover and read-replica routing address latency symptoms but not the root cause; adding capacity fights a regression that may worsen; enabling circuit breakers now, during peak settlement writes, would risk dropping the very transactions we must preserve. Rollback is fast, targeted, and, per b1, reversible with no impact if the release is in fact innocent. If the p99 climb persists after rollback, the next intervention window should revisit capacity or read-replica routing.
